headline: Draft prevention section of homelessness strategic plan reviewed; MaineHousing client funds end December 2026.
summary: About $200,000 of the $350,000 received from MaineHousing paid for client help, such as furnishings and eviction prevention. That client funding ends in December 2026, and the city is asking MaineHousing whether unspent funds can carry over. Draft edits add training for hospital and jail staff and a placeholder for families and youth. The committee also approved its three-month report to go to council.
decisions: Approved the three-month report to go to council.
discussion: Discharge planning: Speakers said people leaving hospitals and jails often have no housing set up, and that case managers may not know all the local resources. They suggested regular training on navigating the system.
Permanent supportive housing: Speakers said the plan needs a common definition of the term and a menu of housing options. One idea was to measure access to housing rather than placements.

Funding for diversion: Some wanted the plan to name the money needed for diversion and client help, while others said to show the data and look for ways to fund it. The group discussed a short list of items that need money to return to later.

Family and youth homelessness: Speakers said Bangor has no family shelters, and some young people who age out of programs such as Shaw House are left on the streets. They asked for a strategy that addresses families and youth.
Strategic plan deadlines: Speakers said dates such as December 31st, 2028 and 2029 are too far off. They suggested deadlines measured from council adoption, such as within 6 months.

decision_evidence.quote: "Yeah, I'd like to motion to pass." ... "With that uh the report has been approved by the committee to go to council."
